headword: {源頼朝|みなもとのよりとも}
gloss: Minamoto no Yoritomo (1147-1199), founder of the Kamakura shogunate

definitions.gloss: Minamoto no Yoritomo, first Kamakura shogun
definitions.explanation: Leader of the Minamoto ({源氏|げんじ}) clan who defeated the Taira ({平家|へいけ}) in the Genpei War and set up Japan's first warrior government, the {鎌倉幕府|かまくらばくふ}, becoming shogun in 1192. His rule began nearly 700 years of government by the samurai class.

examples.japanese: {源頼朝|みなもとのよりとも}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鎌倉|かまくら}→鎌倉：30711_kamakura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{幕府|ばくふ}→幕府：12448_bakufu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: Minamoto no Yoritomo established a shogunate in Kamakura.

examples.japanese: {頼朝|よりとも}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{義経|よしつね}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{対立|たいりつ}した→対立する：22172_tairitsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Yoritomo came into conflict with his younger brother Yoshitsune.

examples.english: I memorized the year Yoritomo became shogun with the phrase "ii kuni tsukurō Kamakura bakufu."

notes:
{源頼朝|みなもとのよりとも} is a fixture of every Japanese history lesson and of historical drama, where he usually appears as a cold, calculating politician.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- ⟦{源義経|みなもとのよしつね}→源義経：31051_minamotonoyoshitsune⟧: his younger brother, the brilliant general who won the war but was hunted down by Yoritomo. Popular sympathy for the doomed Yoshitsune gave rise to the word {判官|ほうがん}びいき (siding with the underdog).
- ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧(1192)つくろう{鎌倉幕府|かまくらばくふ}: the classic mnemonic for the date; many textbooks now date the shogunate from 1185 instead.
- {北条政子|ほうじょうまさこ}: his wife, who held power after his death.
